_comment: Copy to zones.json and describe YOUR network. Zones are matched by longest-prefix, so a specific carve-out (10.30.1.0/24 = tier0) correctly wins over the broad block that contains it (10.0.0.0/8).
_trustTiers: 0 = control plane (DCs, PAWs, OOB mgmt) | 1 = servers | 2 = perimeter/DMZ | 3 = user workstations | 4 = untrusted (guest, BYOD)
_roles: user | server | tier0 | management | dmz | ot | untrusted

zones.name: Domain Controllers and Privileged Access Workstations
zones.description: Identity control plane. Nothing below tier 1 should reach this over an admin protocol.

zones.name: Out-of-Band Management
zones.description: Jump hosts, BMC/iLO/iDRAC, switch management. Should ride a separate path from production traffic.

zones.name: DMZ
zones.description: Internet-facing. Treat any inbound path from here to an internal zone as critical.

zones.name: Corporate Workstations
zones.description: Workstation-to-workstation SMB/RDP has no legitimate business use in most estates and is the primary ransomware propagation path.

zones.name: Plant Floor / ICS
zones.description: SAFE MODE. Controllers can fault on unexpected TCP connects. Active probing requires both activeProbing=true here AND the --allow-ot-probing flag.

unclassifiedZone.name: Unclassified
unclassifiedZone.description: Anything matching no CIDR above. A large unclassified population is itself a finding: NSA's Network and Environment pillar names data flow mapping as the capability segmentation depends on, and you cannot segment what you have not inventoried.
